topic.title: Identifiers
topic.description: Rules for naming variables, methods, and classes

sections.title: What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Ever wondered how programmers name their variables, methods, or classes? • What identifiers are and why they matter
• The dos and don'ts of naming things in Java
• How to make your code readable and professional

sections.title: Core Concepts
sections.content:
Imagine you're labeling boxes in a warehouse. Each box needs a unique, clear name so workers know what's inside. Identifiers are like those labels for your code!

In Java, identifiers are names you give to:
• Variables (like `age` or `totalPrice`)
• Methods (like `calculateTax()`)
• Classes (like `Student` or `BankAccount`)

**Rules to follow:**
• Must start with a letter (a-z, A-Z), underscore (`_`), or dollar sign (`$`)
• Can include letters, digits, underscores, or dollar signs after the first character
• Cannot be a Java keyword (like `int`, `class`, or `public`)
• Case-sensitive (`age` ≠ `Age` ≠ `AGE`)

sections.title: Code Examples
Key Points
points: Identifiers are names for variables, methods, classes, and other program elements
Identifiers must start with a letter, underscore, or dollar sign (not a digit)
Java identifiers are case-sensitive: myVar and myvar are different identifiers
Reserved words (if, class, int, etc.) cannot be used as identifiers
Choose descriptive identifiers that convey the purpose of the element

sections.title: Summary
sections.content: Identifiers are names for variables, methods, and classes. Must start with a letter, `_`, or `$` (no digits or keywords!) Practice naming things clearly and consistently. Ready to learn about variables next.
